target_customer: Pharma partners and patients with neuropsychiatric conditions such as depression and anhedonia (future drug buyers)
problem: Psychedelics have therapeutic promise but come with hallucinations. Mindstate aims to decompose and recombine psychoactive effects to design drugs that deliver therapeutic effects without hallucinations.
business_model: Drug development, preclinical and clinical programs aimed at licensing or commercializing therapeutics

founders.name: Dillan DiNardo
founders.background_notes: YC page: background in venture capital, Fortune 500 M&A and founding biology platforms.

founders.name: Tom Ray
founders.background_notes: YC page: professor of biology and computer science at the University of Oklahoma.

competitors.name: MindMed
competitors.what: Psychedelic medicines including a non-hallucinogenic ibogaine-based candidate

technical_complexity.rationale: Linking molecular biology and human experience to design drugs requires clinical trials, regulatory approval and unproven science.

defensibility.rationale: Patents, trial data and a proprietary experience dataset could be defensible if clinical results hold.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors pursued adjacent approaches; no copying of the decomposition method was found.

market_need_then: Depression and related disorders have large unmet need and psychedelic funding surged in 2021; hallucinations limit use of classic psychedelics.

identity.visual_style: Minimal, sparse layout with abstract science imagery such as eyes, neurons and desert dunes

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: Experience is an engineerable output of biology
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of the funding in Axios and Business Insider headlines on its site

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct positioning and notable press such as Fast Company and Axios, but the name is descriptive and shares words with other mind-themed brands.

outcome_analysis: Mindstate raised an $11.5M seed in February 2022 led by Initialized Capital shortly after the YC Summer 2021 batch and by 2024 and 2025 headlines described a first AI derived psychedelic heading to the clinic and an early FDA nod. A later Series A is reported only by aggregators, so progress and funding after 2022 are unverified; the company remains a preclinical or early clinical biotech whose outcome depends on trial results.
notes: Technical.ly fetch was rate limited, so the seed details rely on a search summary plus the company site headlines (Axios and Business Insider cite 11.5M). One aggregator lists a 12.7M Series A in November 2024 and totals of 12M to 25M; unverified, not recorded. A CB Insights page names Tom Ray as founder while YC and the company site list DiNardo as CEO and Ray as co-founder. Competitor sources for Compass and MindMed are undated. YC lists San Francisco; Technical.ly describes it as Pittsburgh based, unreconciled.
